requirement:
The bundled languages report each recognized source comment as `Comment` on
the item that owns it under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Each comment in a run has its own span and the run's owner. Consumers interpret
the comment text.
rationale: In `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs`, extend `bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax` or add a test marked `{test}` for `requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.comments`. For each bundled comment language other than Rust and Python (TypeScript/TSX, CSS, YAML, TOML, Markdown), assert which outline item owns each reported comment, not only the flattened list of comment spans. Cover at least a run of consecutive comments, such as TOML `# first` and `# second`, which must share the owner of the next item. Cover a trailing comment, which must belong to the innermost item containing its line. Also cover a standalone comment with no following sibling, which must belong to its container. — The requirement says the bundled languages report each recognized comment as `Comment` on the item that owns it under `requirements.references.outline_comments`. Each comment in a run must also have its own span and the run's owner. Two tests are marked. `rust_attachments_keep_the_owner_kind_and_original_bytes` checks the root owner of `//! file docs`, the two-comment `///` run and the trailing comment all on `fn f`, and the separate non-overlapping spans. `bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax` asserts ownership only for Python, where `def[f]` has 3 attachments, and `class.py` also checks the `class[C]` annotation span. For TypeScript, TSX, CSS, YAML, TOML and Markdown it flattens `items.iter().flat_map(|i| &i.attachments)` and compares only (kind, text) pairs. That would accept an implementation for any of those languages that reports the right comment spans but attaches them to the wrong item, such as the root, or to the wrong sibling. It would also accept one that gives a run or a trailing comment the wrong owner. The owner is a stated obligation of the subject, so those languages have no owner evidence.

text: :::{req} attachments.comments
The bundled languages report each recognized source comment as `Comment` on
the item that owns it under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Each comment in a run has its own span and the run's owner. Consumers interpret
the comment text.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. Habeas MUST retain the
one-based line and UTF-8 byte column of each inline role’s opening brace or
fenced reference’s first opening colon. When siblings share a line, the
reference belongs to the item owning the comment at that position. A reference
in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.

output.rationale: The only structural obligation in the text is the reporting shape: "report each recognized source comment as `Comment` on the item that owns it", where "Each comment in a run has its own span and the run's owner". An implementation that attached comments with another kind, such as `Annotation`, or merged a run into one span would break this clause. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#impl[Outline]#2/fn[from_legacy]` meets it. It loops over `outline.comments` and pushes one `OutlineAttachment` per comment onto `items[comment.owner]`. Each has `kind: AttachmentKind::Comment` and the comment's own `byte_start`/`byte_end` span. The `Comment` variant itself is declared in `enum[AttachmentKind]`, which is marked as implementing its own requirement. The decision about which item owns a comment, and how runs form, belongs to the cited `requirements.references.outline_comments`. It is not part of this subject. "Consumers interpret the comment text" is a behavioral statement and needs no structural evidence. `from_legacy` is the only root supplied, and it is marked.
